task1.title: Overseas visitors to the UK
task1.prompt: The graph below shows the number of overseas visitors who went to the UK for different purposes between 1989 and 2009.

chartDesc.title: The number of overseas visitors who went to the UK for different purposes, 1989 - 2009
chartDesc.overview: Holiday was the most common reason for visiting the UK throughout most of the period, while all three categories (Holiday, Business, and Meeting friends and relatives) overall increased between 1989 and 2009.
unreadable: Exact year values for intermediate vertex points between the 5-year axis labels are not explicitly printed.
keyFeatures: Holiday visits were highest overall, starting at 6.5 million in 1989 and peaking at 9 million in both 1994 and 2009.
Visits to meet friends and relatives showed an overall upward trend from 3.5 million in 1989 to 6 million in 2009.
Business travel grew from 5 million in 1989 to 7 million in 2009, briefly overtaking holiday visits around 2007.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparison where relevant.
task1.sampleBand5:
The line graph shows how many visitors went to the UK. It is about from 1989 to 2009 for different things.

The numbers for holiday and business was more than visiting friends and other. Holiday went up and down a bit, from about 10 million to about 15 million. Business was nearly the same, but it was not so high. Visiting friends went up a little bit.

The 'other' line was very low. It started at under 3 million and finished at about 5 million. Holiday was the most popular reason for people to come to the UK.

Overall, the number of visitors changed a little bit in this time.
task1.sampleBand6:
The line graph shows the number of overseas visitors to the UK for three different reasons between 1989 and 2009.

Overall, the number of visitors increased over the period. Visiting friends and relatives was the most popular reason, while business trips were the least popular.

In 1989, around 9 million people visited friends and relatives. This number fluctuated somewhat before rising to about 15 million in 2009. Holidays also increased, from roughly 6 million in 1989 to around 11 million in 2009. There was a general upward trend, but with some periods of decline.

Business visits started at around 2 million in 1989. This remained relatively stable for the first few years, but then experienced a gradual increase to just over 4 million in 2009. The number of business travellers was significantly lower than those visiting for holidays or to see friends and family, and its growth was more modest.
task1.sampleBand7:
The line graph illustrates the fluctuations in the number of overseas visitors to the UK between 1989 and 2009, categorized by purpose of visit: business, holiday, and visiting friends or relatives.

Overall, the number of holiday visitors experienced the most significant growth, while business visits showed a more modest increase. Visits to friends and relatives remained relatively stable over the entire period.

In 1989, holiday visits started at approximately 4 million, and then exhibited an upward trend, reaching a peak of around 12 million in 2009. Business visits also increased, albeit at a slower pace, from roughly 2 million to about 5 million during the same timeframe. By contrast, the number of people visiting friends and relatives fluctuated slightly, hovering around the 4 million mark throughout the two decades, with no discernible long-term pattern.

It is also noticeable that holiday visits consistently surpassed the other two categories, indicating its popularity as the primary reason for overseas visitors to travel to the UK. While business and visiting friends/relatives purposes also saw increases, their growth was significantly less pronounced in comparison to holiday visits.
task1.sampleBand8:
The line graph illustrates the fluctuations in the number of overseas visitors travelling to the UK for leisure, business, and other purposes over a 20-year period, from 1989 to 2009.

Overall, the number of visitors for leisure experienced the most significant growth, while visits for business and other reasons also increased, albeit at a slower rate. It is also immediately apparent that leisure was consistently the most popular reason for visiting the UK throughout the period.

In 1989, approximately 5 million people visited the UK for leisure purposes. This figure witnessed a steady climb to reach a peak of just over 12 million in 2009, representing a substantial increase. Business-related visits started at around 2 million in 1989 and rose gradually to approximately 4 million by 2009. Visits for other purposes also showed an upward trend, beginning at around 1 million and reaching approximately 3 million by the end of the period.

Although all three categories experienced growth, the disparity in the rate of increase is striking. The number of leisure visitors more than doubled, considerably outpacing the growth in business and other visits. This suggests a growing preference for the UK as a tourist destination during the timeframe outlined.
task1.sampleBand9:
The line graph illustrates the fluctuations in the number of overseas visitors to the UK between 1989 and 2009, categorized by the purpose of their visit: business, leisure, and visiting friends or relatives.

Overall, the number of visitors increased over the period, with leisure consistently being the predominant reason for travel. While visits for business and to see friends and relatives also grew, their growth was less pronounced than that of leisure travel. Furthermore, all three categories experienced periods of relative stagnation or decline.

Specifically, leisure visits started at approximately 10 million in 1989 and witnessed a steady climb to reach a peak of around 30 million in 2009. Business visits, in contrast, began at roughly 2 million and experienced a more gradual increase, peaking at around 5 million towards the end of the period. Visits to friends and relatives also showed an upward trend, starting at around 4 million and concluding the period at approximately 8 million. It is worth noting that all three categories experienced a noticeable dip around 2002-2003, possibly reflecting the impact of global events at that time. However, each quickly regained momentum thereafter, with leisure exhibiting the most robust recovery. The disparity in growth rates between leisure and the other two categories became increasingly apparent over the two decades, suggesting a shift in the primary motivations for overseas travel to the UK. In essence, the data suggests a growing tourism industry.
task1.sampleAnswer:
The line graph illustrates the number of international visitors to the UK for three different purposes—holidays, business, and visiting friends and relatives—over a twenty-year period from 1989 to 2009. Overall, all three categories showed an upward trend, with holiday visits consistently attracting the most visitors throughout the period.

In 1989, approximately 10 million people visited the UK for holidays, making it the most popular reason for travel. This figure rose steadily, reaching around 15 million by 1999 and peaking at roughly 18 million in 2009. Business visits started at about 6 million in 1989 and grew gradually to approximately 10 million by 2009, maintaining its position as the second most common purpose for visiting.

Visits to friends and relatives began at the lowest level, with around 4 million visitors in 1989. However, this category experienced the most significant proportional growth, nearly tripling to approximately 11 million by 2009. By the end of the period, the gap between business and VFR (visiting friends and relatives) visits had narrowed considerably, with both categories at similar levels.
task1.uzSampleBand5:
Chiziqli grafika Buyuk Britaniyaga qancha tashrif buyuruvchi kelganini ko'rsatadi. Bu haqida 1989-yildan 2009-yilgacha turli sabablarga ko'ra.

Ta'til va biznes uchun sonlar do'stlarni ziyorat qilish va boshqa sabablarga ko'ra ko'proq edi. Ta'til biroz ko'tarilib tushdi, taxminan 10 milliondan 15 milliongacha. Biznes deyarli bir xil edi, lekin u unchalik yuqori emas edi. Do'stlarni ziyorat qilish biroz ko'tarildi.

'Boshqa' chiziq juda past edi. U 3 milliondan kamdan boshlanib, taxminan 5 millionda tugadi. Ta'til Buyuk Britaniyaga odamlarning kelishining eng mashhur sababi edi.

Umuman olganda, tashrif buyuruvchilar soni bu vaqt ichida biroz o'zgardi.
task1.uzSampleBand6:
Chiziqli grafika 1989 yildan 2009 yilgacha Buyuk Britaniyaga kelgan xorijlik mehmonlar sonini uch xil sababga ko'ra ko'rsatadi.

Umuman olganda, tashrif buyuruvchilar soni davr mobaynida oshdi. Do'stlar va qarindoshlarni ziyorat qilish eng mashhur sabab bo'lgan bo'lsa, biznes safarlari eng kam mashhur bo'lgan.

1989 yilda taxminan 9 million kishi do'stlari va qarindoshlarini ziyorat qilgan. Bu raqam 2009 yilda taxminan 15 millionga ko'tarilishidan oldin biroz o'zgarib turdi. Ta'tillar ham oshdi, 1989 yildagi taxminan 6 milliondan 2009 yilda taxminan 11 millionga yetdi. Umumiy o'sish tendentsiyasi kuzatildi, ammo ba'zi pasayish davrlari ham bo'lgan.

Biznes tashriflari 1989 yilda taxminan 2 milliondan boshlangan. Bu dastlabki bir necha yil davomida nisbatan barqaror bo'lib qoldi, ammo keyin asta-sekin o'sishni boshladi va 2009 yilda 4 milliondan sal ko'proqni tashkil etdi. Biznes sayohatchilar soni ta'tilga yoki do'stlar va oilani ko'rish uchun tashrif buyurganlardan ancha kam edi va uning o'sishi ancha kamtarona bo'ldi.
task1.uzSampleBand7:
Chiziqli grafik 1989 yildan 2009 yilgacha bo'lgan davrda Buyuk Britaniyaga xorijiy tashrif buyuruvchilar sonidagi o'zgarishlarni tasvirlaydi, tashrif maqsadi bo'yicha tasniflangan: biznes, ta'til va do'stlar yoki qarindoshlarni ziyorat qilish.

Umuman olganda, ta'til tashriflari soni eng katta o'sishni ko'rsatdi, biznes tashriflari esa unchalik katta bo'lmagan o'sishni namoyon qildi. Do'stlar va qarindoshlarga tashriflar butun davr mobaynida nisbatan barqaror bo'lib qoldi.

1989 yilda ta'til tashriflari taxminan 4 milliondan boshlandi va keyin o'sish tendentsiyasini namoyish etdi, 2009 yilda taxminan 12 millionga yetdi. Biznes tashriflari ham o'sdi, ammo sekinroq sur'atda, xuddi shu vaqt oralig'ida taxminan 2 milliondan 5 milliongacha. Aksincha, do'stlar va qarindoshlarni ziyorat qiluvchilar soni biroz o'zgarib turdi va ikki o'n yillik davomida 4 million atrofida bo'lib, hech qanday aniq uzoq muddatli tendentsiya kuzatilmadi.

Shuningdek, ta'til tashriflari doimiy ravishda ustun kelgani ham e'tiborga loyiq, bu Buyuk Britaniyaga xorijiy tashrif buyuruvchilar uchun asosiy sabab sifatida uning mashhurligini ko'rsatadi. Biznes va do'stlar/qarindoshlarni ziyorat qilish maqsadlari ham o'sishni ko'rsatgan bo'lsa-da, ularning o'sishi ta'til tashriflariga nisbatan sezilarli darajada kamroq edi.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Chiziqli grafika 1989-yildan 2009-yilgacha bo'lgan 20 yillik davr mobaynida Buyuk Britaniyaga dam olish, biznes va boshqa maqsadlarda sayohat qiluvchi xorijiy sayyohlar sonidagi tebranishlarni ko'rsatadi.

Umuman olganda, dam olish uchun kelgan sayyohlar soni eng sezilarli o'sishni boshdan kechirdi, biznes va boshqa sabablarga ko'ra tashriflar ham oshdi, garchi sekinroq sur'atlarda bo'lsa ham. Shuningdek, shuni darhol anglash mumkinki, dam olish butun davr mobaynida Buyuk Britaniyaga tashrif buyurishning eng mashhur sababi bo'lgan.

1989-yilda taxminan 5 million kishi dam olish maqsadida Buyuk Britaniyaga tashrif buyurgan. Bu ko'rsatkich doimiy ravishda o'sib bordi va 2009-yilda 12 milliondan sal ko'proq cho'qqiga chiqdi, bu sezilarli o'sishni anglatadi. Biznes bilan bog'liq tashriflar 1989-yilda taxminan 2 milliondan boshlangan va asta-sekin o'sib, 2009-yilga kelib taxminan 4 millionga yetgan. Boshqa maqsadlarda tashriflar ham o'sish tendentsiyasini ko'rsatdi, taxminan 1 milliondan boshlanib, davr oxiriga kelib taxminan 3 millionga yetdi.

Garchi barcha uchta toifa o'sishni boshdan kechirgan bo'lsa-da, o'sish sur'atidagi tafovut hayratlanarli. Dam oluvchi sayyohlar soni ikki barobardan ko'proqqa oshdi, bu biznes va boshqa tashriflardagi o'sishdan ancha o'zib ketdi. Bu ko'rsatilgan vaqt oralig'ida Buyuk Britaniyaning sayyohlik maskani sifatida o'sib borayotgan afzalligini ko'rsatadi.
task1.uzSampleBand9:
Chiziqli grafikda Buyuk Britaniyaga 1989-yildan 2009-yilgacha bo'lgan davrda tashrif buyuruvchi xorijliklar sonining o'zgarishlari aks ettirilgan, tashrif maqsadi bo'yicha toifalarga bo'lingan: biznes, dam olish va do'stlar yoki qarindoshlarni ziyorat qilish.

Umuman olganda, tashrif buyuruvchilar soni davr mobaynida oshdi, dam olish esa doimiy ravishda sayohat uchun asosiy sabab bo'lib qoldi. Biznes uchun va do'stlar va qarindoshlarni ko'rish uchun tashriflar ham o'sgan bo'lsa-da, ularning o'sishi dam olish sayohatiga qaraganda unchalik sezilarli emas edi. Bundan tashqari, barcha uchta toifa nisbatan turg'unlik yoki pasayish davrlarini boshdan kechirdi.

Xususan, dam olish tashriflari 1989-yilda taxminan 10 milliondan boshlanib, doimiy o'sishni kuzatdi va 2009-yilda taxminan 30 millionga yetdi. Biznes tashriflari esa, aksincha, taxminan 2 milliondan boshlanib, asta-sekin o'sishni boshdan kechirdi va davr oxiriga kelib taxminan 5 millionga yetdi. Do'stlar va qarindoshlarga tashriflar ham o'sish tendentsiyasini ko'rsatdi, taxminan 4 milliondan boshlanib, davrni yakunladi taxminan 8 million bilan. Shuni ta'kidlash joizki, barcha uchta toifa 2002-2003-yillarda sezilarli pasayishni boshdan kechirdi, bu o'sha paytdagi global voqealarning ta'sirini aks ettirishi mumkin. Biroq, har biri tezda shundan keyin sur'atni tikladi, dam olish eng mustahkam tiklanishni namoyish etdi. Dam olish va boshqa ikkita toifa o'rtasidagi o'sish sur'atlaridagi tafovut ikki o'n yillik davomida tobora yaqqolroq bo'lib bordi, bu esa Buyuk Britaniyaga xorijiy sayohatlar uchun asosiy motivatsiyalarda o'zgarish borligini ko'rsatadi. Aslida, ma'lumotlar o'sib borayotgan turizm sanoatini ko'rsatadi.

task2.title: Executive vs employee salaries
task2.prompt: Directors of large organizations earn much higher salaries than ordinary employees do. Some people think it is necessary, but others are of the opinion that it is unfair. Discuss both these views and give your opinion.
task2.instruction: Discuss both these views and give your opinion.
task2.sampleBand5:
It is true that in big companies, the bosses get paid a lot more than the people who work for them. Some people think this is okay, but others think it's not fair. I am going to write about both sides and then say what I think.

Some people say that it's necessary for the directors to get so much money. They say that it is a hard job and they have a lot of responsibility. They have to make big decisions for the company, and if they make the wrong decisions, the company could lose money or even go out of business. So, they need to be paid a lot to make sure they do a good job. Also, if they didn't get paid so much, then maybe they would go and work for another company. So they get a lot of money to stay.

However, other people think that it is unfair that the bosses get so much money. They say that the ordinary workers are the ones who are doing all the hard work and that the bosses are just sitting in their offices. Also the workers don't get much money. They might be struggling to pay their bills, while the bosses are living in luxury. They think it would be better if the money was shared more fairly between everyone in the company, then people will be happy.

In my opinion, I think it's a bit of both. I think that the bosses should get paid more because they have more responsibility. But I also think that the gap between the bosses and the workers is too big. I think that companies should try to make sure that everyone is paid a fair wage.
task2.sampleBand6:
It is a common situation that directors of big companies are paid much more than their employees. There are different opinions about this. Some people think it is a necessary thing, while others believe it is not fair. This essay will discuss both points of view and then I will give my own opinion.

On the one hand, some argue that high salaries for directors are justified. The main reason for this is that these people have a lot of responsibility. They are in charge of making important decisions that can affect the whole company and the jobs of many workers. If they make good choices, the company can be very successful. Also, it is often said that these high salaries attract the best people for the job. If the pay wasn’t so good, the most talented managers might go to work for other companies.

However, others think that the big difference in pay between directors and ordinary workers is unfair. They say that all employees contribute to the success of the company, not just the directors. It can also be argued that these high salaries create a gap between the rich and the poor. Workers might feel undervalued and not motivated if they know that the directors are earning so much more than them. Furthermore, some people believe that very high salaries can lead to greed and corruption.

In my opinion, while it is important to pay directors well to attract talent and reward responsibility, the difference between their salaries and the salaries of ordinary workers should not be too big. I think it is important to find a balance that is fair to everyone and motivates all employees to work hard for the success of the company. Perhaps more profit-sharing schemes would be a good idea.
task2.sampleBand7:
It is often observed that directors of large corporations receive significantly higher salaries compared to their average employees. This disparity in income sparks debate, with some arguing it is justified, while others deem it unjust. This essay will explore both perspectives before presenting my own view.

Proponents of high executive pay often contend that it is a necessary incentive to attract and retain top talent. The rationale is that leading large organizations requires exceptional skills, experience, and decision-making abilities. The responsibilities are immense, and the pressure to deliver results is constant. Therefore, substantial compensation packages, including high salaries and bonuses, are seen as a way to reward performance and motivate executives to drive company growth. Furthermore, the argument goes, the success of a company often hinges on the strategic vision of its leaders, and this contribution warrants significant financial reward.

Conversely, critics argue that the vast difference between executive pay and that of ordinary workers is fundamentally unfair. They point out that the success of a company is a collective effort, and that all employees, from the top down, contribute to its performance. A disproportionate allocation of profits to a small group of executives can be demoralizing for the workforce and create a sense of injustice. Some also suggest that excessive executive pay is not necessarily linked to improved company performance and that alternative compensation models, such as profit-sharing schemes, could be more equitable and motivating for all employees.

In my opinion, while recognizing the need to attract capable leaders with competitive salaries, the current level of disparity is often excessive. A more balanced approach is needed, where executive compensation is tied more closely to long-term company performance and the well-being of all employees. While high-level executives possess important skills, the value of *every* employee should be recognised through fairer wages. Greater transparency and accountability in executive pay decisions are also essential to ensure that compensation reflects genuine contribution and avoids the perception of greed and inequality.
task2.sampleBand8:
The disparity in remuneration between senior executives and ordinary employees in large organizations is a subject of considerable debate. While some argue that such high salaries are justified, others consider them to be fundamentally unfair. This essay will examine both perspectives before presenting my own view.

Proponents of high executive pay often contend that it is a necessary incentive to attract and retain top talent. The reasoning is that the responsibilities and pressures associated with leading large corporations are immense, requiring exceptional skills, experience, and dedication. They believe that commensurate compensation is required to motivate individuals to take on such challenging roles and to ensure that they remain committed to the organization. Moreover, high salaries can be seen as a reflection of the value that successful executives bring to a company, driving profitability, innovation, and market share, thereby benefiting shareholders and employees alike. Furthermore, the competitive market for executive talent dictates that companies must offer attractive packages to secure the best candidates.

Conversely, critics argue that the vast pay gap between executives and ordinary workers is unjustifiable and contributes to growing income inequality. They point out that while executives are undoubtedly important, the success of a company depends on the collective effort of all employees, from the boardroom to the factory floor. It is argued that the dedication and hard work of ordinary employees are often undervalued and undercompensated, especially when compared to the exorbitant salaries and bonuses awarded to executives. Furthermore, some argue that high executive pay is often linked to short-term performance metrics, which can incentivize risky or unethical behavior that ultimately harms the company and its stakeholders. In addition to this, there is a perception that executive compensation is often determined by self-serving boards of directors, who are more concerned with maintaining their own positions and benefits than with fairly distributing wealth.

In my opinion, while it is important to appropriately reward executives for their contributions, the current level of disparity in many organizations is excessive and unsustainable. A more equitable distribution of wealth, which takes into account the contributions of all employees, is not only fairer but also likely to foster greater employee engagement, loyalty, and productivity. Ultimately, a balance must be struck between incentivizing top talent and ensuring a fair and just compensation system for all.
task2.sampleBand9:
The disparity in remuneration between directors of large corporations and their ordinary employees is a subject of considerable debate. While some argue that such high salaries are justified and necessary, others deem them to be inherently unfair. This essay will explore both sides of this complex issue before offering a reasoned opinion.

Proponents of high executive pay frequently contend that it is essential for attracting and retaining top talent. They argue that the responsibilities and pressures associated with leading a major organization are immense, demanding exceptional skills and experience. In this line of reasoning, substantial compensation packages, including generous salaries, bonuses, and stock options, are necessary to incentivize individuals with the requisite capabilities to take on these challenging roles and maximize shareholder value. Furthermore, the performance of a company is often directly linked to the decisions and strategies implemented by its leadership, and therefore, it stands to reason that those who drive success should be handsomely rewarded. A failure to offer competitive salaries could result in a drain of talent to rival companies, ultimately harming the organization's long-term prospects.

Conversely, critics argue that the vast pay gap between executives and ordinary workers is ethically indefensible and economically unsustainable. They point out that while directors often enjoy exorbitant salaries, many employees struggle to make ends meet, even with full-time employment. This disparity can lead to feelings of resentment and demoralization among the workforce, potentially impacting productivity and overall morale. Moreover, some argue that executive compensation is often detached from actual performance, with directors receiving large bonuses even when the company is underperforming. This perceived lack of accountability fuels public outrage and contributes to a growing sense of inequality. It is also suggested that more equitable distribution of wealth within an organization could lead to a more engaged and motivated workforce, fostering a more collaborative and productive environment.

In conclusion, while there is a valid argument to be made for incentivizing and rewarding exceptional leadership, the current level of disparity between executive pay and that of ordinary employees is, in my opinion, excessive and unsustainable. A more balanced approach is needed, one that recognizes the value of both leadership and workforce contributions, and promotes a fairer distribution of wealth within organizations. Ultimately, a more equitable system would benefit not only employees but also the long-term health and stability of the companies themselves.
task2.sampleAnswer:
The significant disparity between the salaries of corporate directors and regular employees is a topic of considerable debate. While some argue that high executive pay is justified, others contend that it is fundamentally unfair. This essay will examine both perspectives before presenting my own view.

Those who support high salaries for directors often point to the immense responsibilities these individuals bear. The decisions made by CEOs and other top executives can determine the fate of entire companies, affecting thousands of jobs and billions in revenue. From this perspective, their compensation reflects the value they bring to the organization and the risks they take. Furthermore, in a competitive global market, companies must offer attractive packages to recruit and retain top talent who might otherwise work for rivals.

On the other hand, critics argue that the pay gap has become excessive and unjustifiable. Many ordinary employees work long hours and contribute significantly to a company's success, yet their wages have stagnated while executive pay has soared. This growing inequality can damage morale, reduce productivity, and contribute to broader social problems. Moreover, studies have shown that exorbitant executive pay does not always correlate with superior company performance, calling into question its supposed meritocratic basis.

In my opinion, while directors should be compensated well for their expertise and accountability, the current level of disparity is often disproportionate and harmful to society. A more balanced approach, perhaps linking executive pay more closely to company-wide performance and employee wages, would be fairer and more sustainable in the long term.
task2.uzSampleBand5:
Katta kompaniyalarda boshliqlar o'z ishchilariga qaraganda ancha ko'p maosh olishi rost. Ba'zi odamlar bu yaxshi deb o'ylashadi, lekin boshqalar bu adolatdan emas deb hisoblashadi. Men ikkala tomon haqida yozmoqchiman va keyin o'z fikrimni aytaman.

Ba'zi odamlar direktorlarga bunchalik ko'p pul berish zarur deb aytishadi. Ular aytishicha, bu qiyin ish va ularning zimmasida katta mas'uliyat bor. Ular kompaniya uchun katta qarorlar qabul qilishlari kerak va agar ular noto'g'ri qarorlar qabul qilsalar, kompaniya pul yo'qotishi yoki hatto biznesdan chiqib ketishi mumkin. Shuning uchun, ular yaxshi ishlashlarini ta'minlash uchun ularga ko'p pul to'lash kerak. Bundan tashqari, agar ularga bunchalik ko'p pul to'lanmasa, ular boshqa kompaniyada ishlashga ketishlari mumkin. Shuning uchun ularga qolishlari uchun ko'p pul beriladi.

Biroq, boshqa odamlar boshliqlarning bunchalik ko'p pul olishi adolatsizlik deb hisoblashadi. Ular aytishicha, oddiy ishchilar butun mashaqqatli mehnatni qiladilar va boshliqlar shunchaki o'z ofislarida o'tirishadi. Shuningdek, ishchilar ko'p pul olishmaydi. Ular to'lovlarni to'lash uchun kurashayotgan bo'lishi mumkin, boshliqlar esa dabdabali hayot kechirishadi. Ularning fikricha, agar pul kompaniyadagi hamma o'rtasida adolatliroq taqsimlansa, odamlar baxtli bo'lishadi.

Mening fikrimcha, bu ikkalasining ham bir qismi. Menimcha, boshliqlar ko'proq pul olishlari kerak, chunki ularning zimmasida ko'proq mas'uliyat bor. Ammo men, shuningdek, boshliqlar va ishchilar o'rtasidagi tafovut juda katta deb o'ylayman. Menimcha, kompaniyalar har bir kishiga adolatli ish haqi to'lanishiga harakat qilishlari kerak.
task2.uzSampleBand6:
Katta kompaniyalar direktorlari o'z xodimlariga qaraganda ancha ko'p maosh olishi odatiy holat. Bu haqda turli xil fikrlar mavjud. Ba'zilar bu zarur narsa deb hisoblasa, boshqalar bu adolatdan emas deb hisoblashadi. Ushbu insho har ikki nuqtai nazarni muhokama qiladi va keyin o'z fikrimni bildiraman.

Bir tomondan, ba'zilar direktorlarning yuqori maoshlari oqlanadi, deb ta'kidlaydi. Buning asosiy sababi shundaki bu odamlar katta mas'uliyatga ega. Ular butun kompaniyaga va ko'plab ishchilarning ish joylariga ta'sir qilishi mumkin bo'lgan muhim qarorlar qabul qilish uchun javobgardir. Agar ular yaxshi tanlov qilsalar, kompaniya juda muvaffaqiyatli bo'lishi mumkin. Shuningdek, ko'pincha aytilishicha bu yuqori maoshlar ish uchun eng yaxshi odamlarni jalb qiladi. Agar maosh bunchalik yaxshi bo'lmasa, eng iste'dodli menejerlar boshqa kompaniyalarda ishlashga ketishi mumkin edi.

Biroq, boshqalar direktorlar va oddiy ishchilar o'rtasidagi maoshdagi katta farq adolatsizlik deb hisoblashadi. Ularning aytishicha, kompaniyaning muvaffaqiyatiga faqat direktorlar emas, balki barcha xodimlar hissa qo'shadi. Shuningdek, ta'kidlash mumkinki bu yuqori maoshlar boylar va kambag'allar o'rtasida tafovut yaratadi. Agar ishchilar direktorlar ulardan ancha ko'p pul topishini bilishsa, o'zlarini qadrsiz his qilishlari va motivatsiyani yo'qotishlari mumkin. Bundan tashqari, ba'zi odamlar ishonishicha juda yuqori maoshlar ochko'zlik va korruptsiyaga olib kelishi mumkin.

Mening fikrimcha, iste'dodlarni jalb qilish va mas'uliyatni taqdirlash uchun direktorlarga yaxshi maosh to'lash muhim bo'lsa-da, ularning maoshlari va oddiy ishchilarning maoshlari o'rtasidagi farq juda katta bo'lmasligi kerak. Menimcha, bu muhim hamma uchun adolatli bo'lgan va barcha xodimlarni kompaniyaning muvaffaqiyati uchun astoydil ishlashga undaydigan muvozanatni topish.
